method.value: Evolve two isolated star clusters (large and small) for 2 Myr using AMUSE coupling N-body (ph4), Tree-SPH (GADGET-2), stellar evolution (SeBA), and stellar winds ('heat' mode) via a Bridge scheme.

findings_qualitative.value: The JVLA 15 and 22 GHz continuum maps show an asymmetric extended ionized envelope dominated by a single bright resolved cluster peak at RA 05:55:42.60 DEC 03:23:32.0 rather than multiple secondary sub-clusters.

evidence.quote: the current data show that ionized gas has an unusual and asymmetric extended structure and that the spatial distribution is dominated by one large cluster.

findings_qualitative.value: Both velocity components of [S IV] appear in every spatial pixel across the source without a separate spatial clump for the red component, indicating that if two distinct clusters exist they overlap along the line of sight.

findings_qualitative.value: Stellar winds are the primary factor shaping the simulated pre-collision clusters, blowing away gas, increasing cluster radii, and distorting the outer regions of the larger cluster while the denser small cluster remains mostly spherical.

evidence.quote: We find that the stellar winds were the most significant factor in shaping the clusters, which is consistent with the results of simulations run by (Pelupessy & Portegies Zwart 2012); they blew away some of the gas particles, resulting in an overall increase of the clusters radii, and a decrease in the gas density, temperature and average rms velocity.

findings_qualitative.value: In the grazing collision model (b = 4 pc), the two clusters are not gravitationally bound to each other and exchange gas across a bridge region that will thin out as the clusters separate unless a new SSC forms.

claims.hypothesis: The asymmetric, double-peaked [S IV] line profile in II Zw 40 is produced by two super star clusters offset in velocity that can be spatially resolved at ~0.1-0.3 arcsec resolution.
claims.experiment: Image the region at 15 and 22 GHz with JVLA (~0.1-0.2 arcsec beam) and map the [S IV] 10.5 um emission cube with Gemini North/TEXES (~0.3 arcsec beam, 4.5 km s^-1 resolution) to search for a spatial clump associated with the red velocity component.
claims.result: Only one distinct radio continuum peak is detected (size 0.13 arcsec, flux 0.59 mJy), and both blue (~744 km s^-1) and red (~775 km s^-1) [S IV] velocity components appear in every pixel with no separate spatial density peak for the red emission.
claims.finding: If two distinct star clusters are present, they overlap so closely along the line of sight that they cannot be spatially separated in the ionized gas maps.

evidence.loc: 4.1 Ionized Gas: Double Peak or Extended Wing?
evidence.quote: We conclude that if there are two distinct clusters, as the [S IV] profile strongly suggests, they so overlap in the line of sight that they cannot be separated.

claims.hypothesis: The supernebula SSC-N in II Zw 40 is located at the collision/overlap of two elongated molecular clouds at different velocities.
claims.experiment: Analyze the ALMA CO(3-2) moment maps, region-summed line profiles, and Position-Velocity Diagrams (PVDs) along RA and Dec, and compare with the [S IV] and radio continuum distributions.
claims.result: The main molecular streamer exhibits two velocity peaks (~745-750 km s^-1 and ~760-772 km s^-1) that merge and reach maximum velocity dispersion at the radio/[S IV] source, and the Dec PVD shows a V-shape / check-mark signature.
claims.finding: The core of II Zw 40 holds two elongated molecular clouds overlapping in the line of sight and colliding on the west end where the embedded star formation is concentrated.

evidence.loc: 4.2 Molecular Gas: Two Elongated Clouds at Different Velocities
evidence.quote: The Position-Velocity diagram (PVD) along the Dec axis resembles the V-shape observational signature of a cloud-cloud collision Torii et al. (2017) (highlighted in a subfigure in Figure 5).
These observations strongly suggest that the clouds are colliding or merging on the west end and that the star formation is concentrated in the collision region.

claims.hypothesis: The spatial and kinematic structures of the II Zw 40 supernebula can be reproduced by a collision between two embedded star clusters of masses 4.5 x 10^5 M_sun and 2.2 x 10^5 M_sun.
claims.experiment: Run AMUSE N-body, SPH, stellar evolution, and stellar wind simulations of two colliding clusters across impact parameters b = 0 to 6 pc, generate synthetic CO(3-2) and [S IV] observations with RADMC-3D at inclinations of 45, 60, and 75 deg, and compare with ALMA and TEXES data.
claims.result: A grazing collision with impact parameter b = 4 pc at timestep T = 0.5 Myr observed at an inclination of 45 deg best matches the shape, spatial/kinematic separation, and peak ratio of the observed CO(3-2) and [S IV] profiles and PVDs.
claims.finding: The supernebula is well explained by a grazing collision in which the smaller, denser cluster distorts the larger cluster and creates an ionized gas bridge between them.

evidence.quote: The model that best agrees with the data is a grazing collision that has distorted the gas and stars to create the distinctive structures observed.
We determine that the best match to the CO and [S IV] observations occurs for the 𝑏 = 4pc impact parameter, at the 𝑇 = 0 . 5Myr timestep, when observed at a 45° inclination angle.

why_this_data.value: [S IV] 10.5 um is less affected by extinction and thermal broadening than H recombination lines, probing ionized gas kinematics at ~4.5 km s^-1 resolution; high-resolution Gemini/TEXES and JVLA data were obtained to test the two-cluster hypothesis from lower-resolution IRTF data, while ALMA CO(3-2) probes the dense warm molecular gas at comparable resolution.

evidence.quote: an ALMA spectral cube of the CO(3-2) line that probes the dense warm molecular gas with spatial and velocity resolution comparable to the ionized gas.

[S IV] has two great advantages over H i recombination lines; it is less affected by extinction than many, including Br 𝛾, and it is much less affected by thermal broadening than any hydrogen line can be.

evidence.quote: Beck et al. (2013) accordingly suggested that two super star clusters offset in velocity were included in the same beam, a model which motivated the higher resolution observations of Gemini.

why_this_method.value: AMUSE was chosen to run N-body gravity, SPH hydrodynamics, stellar evolution, and stellar winds in parallel via a Bridge scheme; the stellar wind 'heat' mode was selected because stellar winds develop differently in dense embedded clusters; clusters were trimmed to slightly over the virial radius and Salpeter IMF restricted to [15, 120] M_sun to keep computational runtime realistic while preserving core structure and wind effects.

evidence.quote: The Astrophysical Multipurpose Software Environment (AMUSE) assembles community codes and makes it possible to run computations of all these aspects in parallel and to communicate the results between codes.
we accordingly use the stellar wind module’s ’heat’ mode, which follows the energy rather than the velocity of the wind particles, as most appropriate for this embedded source.
The clusters were then trimmed to a little over the virial radius of each (which was also higher than the half-mass radius).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Multiple secondary sub-clusters seen in earlier radio maps (Beck et al. 2002; Kepley et al. 2014) were found to be ~2 sigma fluctuations or deconvolution artifacts when deeper JVLA maps revealed a single dominant cluster with asymmetric extended emission.

evidence.quote: Where Beck et al. (2002) saw ≈ 2 𝜎 brightness fluctuations as possible secondary clusters and could not detect most of the extended emission, the current data show that ionized gas has an unusual and asymmetric extended structure and that the spatial distribution is dominated by one large cluster.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Alternative explanations for why the small cluster lies on the outer edge of the [S IV] distribution: (1) the small clump contained no stars prior to the collision, or (2) a new SSC formed in the bridge area relatively closer to the large cluster's core.

evidence.quote: (We intend in future work to examine separately the alternate case of star formation starting after the collision).

how_they_decided_enough.value: Cluster evolution time (2 Myr) was set by the maximum dynamical relaxation time of the gas; SPH particle mass (1.5 M_sun) was chosen by convergence testing of cluster evolution runs; impact parameter grid was stopped at b = 6 pc where cluster interaction becomes minimal.

limitations_admitted.value: Magnetic field effects are omitted from the simulations due to lack of observational data.

evidence.quote: (and ideally the magnetic field, for which there is at present no data).
As the initial model was very general (with the one major omission of not yet including magnetic field effects) we expect these findings to be valid for typical clusters.

limitations_admitted.value: Low-mass stars (< 15 M_sun) are omitted from the Salpeter IMF to keep computational demands realistic.

evidence.quote: We chose these ’top heavy’ mass limits to keep the total stellar mass and the computational demands realistic; the winds of low mass stars are so much weaker than those of massive stars that they can be omitted with little effect on the large-scale results.

limitations_admitted.value: The simulations do not explicitly model the elongated molecular clouds, their chemistry/cooling, or their interactions with the stars and ionized gas, nor do they include accretion, fragmentation, or ongoing star formation.

limitations_admitted.value: The simulations cannot currently distinguish whether the star clusters formed before the collision or as a result of the cloud collision.

evidence.quote: The major unanswered question is whether the star clusters were formed before the collision as we posited here, or are a result of the collision of two clouds. As the upper range of the age of SSC-N is 3Myr Vanzi et al. (2008), both options are at present valid and the simulations cannot at present distinguish.

referee_caveats_inferred: Synthetic CO(3-2) and [S IV] emission in RADMC-3D are generated from the same isothermal (initially 10^4 K) SPH gas distribution without explicit multiphase ISM thermodynamics, molecular chemistry, or photoionization modeling.

The initial relative collision velocity (~120 km s^-1) is much higher than the observed line-of-sight velocity separation (~25-30 km s^-1) even at a 45 deg viewing inclination, and the gravitational binding or galactic potential driving such a high relative velocity in a dwarf galaxy is not dynamically modeled.
Model selection (b = 4 pc, T = 0.5 Myr, i = 45 deg) is performed by qualitative visual inspection rather than a quantitative goodness-of-fit metric.

data_public_as_stated.value: Observational data are publicly available at the NRAO, ALMA, and Gemini North archives.

evidence.quote: The data used in this paper are available to the public at the archives of the observatories where they were obtained: the radio continuum data is on the NRAO archive, the molecular data at the ALMA archive, and the [S IV] data is at Gemini North.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-50 GB (one Early Science ALMA Band 7 project 2013.1.00122.S, two short JVLA continuum executions, one Gemini/TEXES spectral cube, plus 3D SPH/RADMC-3D simulation grids)
reproducibility.score_reason: Raw observational datasets (ALMA, JVLA, Gemini) are public and basic observational metrics (flux, size, line velocities) can be re-measured from the cubes/maps, but ALMA imaging parameters are largely omitted (likely inherited from Consiglio et al. 2016/2017) and the AMUSE/RADMC-3D simulation scripts and several initial condition / radiative transfer parameters are not released.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: All observational data (ALMA 2013.1.00122.S, JVLA 16B-067, Gemini GN-2017A-Q-57) are public in observatory archives, and the primary observational measurements (22 GHz clump size and flux, [S IV] and CO(3-2) velocity components and PVDs) can be directly reproduced from the archival data.
